purpose: Track a two-cycle flux class through puncturing of a tetrahedral sphere and identify its boundary/cap record.

closedFlux.conclusion: The constant outward face flux is a non-exact H2 representative on the closed tetrahedral sphere.

puncture.conclusion: After puncturing, the retained flux is exact. Its integral becomes the circulation on the new boundary; the removed cap flux is the additional gluing record needed to reconstruct total closed flux.

physicalBoundary.sourceFreeMaxwell: On a closed sphere bounding a volume, d2 B=0 forces total magnetic flux to zero.
physicalBoundary.nonzeroExample: The nonzero H2 class is a topological/cochain example; electromagnetically it requires magnetic charge, a deleted interior, or a non-bounding two-cycle such as a torus sector.
physicalBoundary.retainedLesson: Whatever its physical source, puncturing moves the bulk H2 record into boundary circulation plus cap/gluing flux.

verdict: The two-cycle analogue of the Wilson cut rule holds exactly: puncturing converts a non-exact closed-surface flux into exact face curvature whose integral is recorded by boundary circulation, while the removed cap carries the remaining gluing datum.
